[[Derry]], [[Northern Ireland]] | capacity = 6,242 | current = 2026 League of Ireland Premier Division | owner = Supporter owned | chairman = Philip O'Doherty | manager = [[Mark Connolly]] (interim) | league = [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] | season = [[2025 League of Ireland Premier Division|2025]] | position = 2nd of 10 | website = {{URL|https://www.derrycityfc.net/|derrycityfc.net}} | pattern_la1 = _derrycity24h | pattern_b1 = _derrycity24h | pattern_ra1 = _derrycity24h | pattern_sh1 = _derrycity24h | pattern_so1 = _derrycity24h | leftarm1 = FF0000 | body1 = FF0000 | rightarm1 = FF0000 | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = FFFFFF | pattern_la2 = _derrycity24a | pattern_b2 = _derrycity24a | pattern_ra2 = _derrycity24a | pattern_sh2 = _derrycity24a | pattern_so2 = _derrycity24a | leftarm2 = 171A49 | body2 = 171A49 | rightarm2 = 171A49 | shorts2 = 171A49 | socks2 = 171A49 }} '''Derry City Football Club''' are a professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Derry]], [[Northern Ireland]]. They play in the [[League of Ireland Premier Division]], the top tier of league football in the [[Republic of Ireland]], and are its only member from Northern Ireland.{{cite web |last1=Willis |first1=Craig |last2=Hughes |first2=Will |last3=Bober |first3=Sergiusz |title=ECMI Minorities Blog. National and Linguistic Minorities in the Context of Professional Football across Europe: Five Examples from Kin-State Situations |url=https://www.ecmi.de/infochannel/detail/ecmi-minorities-blog-national-and-linguistic-minorities-in-the-context-of-professional-football-across-europe-five-examples-from-kin-state-situations |website=ECMI |access-date=21 June 2023}} The club's home ground is the [[Brandywell Stadium|Brandywell]]. Derry City wear red and white striped shirts from which their nickname, '''the Candystripes''', derives.{{Cite web |title=Albionroad.com |url=http://albionroad.com/club-histories/the-history-of-derry-city.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305145152/http://albionroad.com/club-histories/the-history-of-derry-city.html |archive-date=2016-03-05 |access-date=2026-01-03 |website=albionroad.com}} The club are also known as '''the Red and White Army''', '''Derry''' or '''City'''.{{cite web|url=http://www.gettogether.at/derry/index.php/content/view/175/101/ |title=Derry City 4–0 Sligo Rovers|access-date=8 June 2007 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928174410/http://www.gettogether.at/derry/index.php/content/view/175/101/ |archive-date=28 September 2007 |work=GetTogether.at|date= 17 October 2006 }} The club, founded in 1928, initially played in the [[IFA Premiership|Irish League]], the domestic league in Northern Ireland, and won a title in [[Irish League 1964–65|1964–65]]. In 1971, security concerns related to [[the Troubles]] meant matches could not be played at the Brandywell and the team had to play home fixtures {{convert|30|mi|km}} away in [[Coleraine]]. While security force objections to the use of the Brandywell were withdrawn the following year, the Irish League insisted that the arrangement, an unsustainable one, continue and the club withdrew from the league. After 13 years in junior football, Derry City joined the League of Ireland's new First Division for 1985–86. They won the First Division title and achieved promotion to the Premier Division in 1987, remaining there until an administrative relegation in 2009. The club won a domestic [[The Treble|treble]] in [[League of Ireland 1988–89|1988–89]].{{cite web|url=https://www.newsletter.co.uk/sport/football/treble-winner-liam-coyle-reflects-on-jim-mclaughlin-s-derry-city-legacy-1-8801143|title=Treble winner Liam Coyle reflects on Jim McLaughlin's Derry City legacy|date=7 February 2019|first=Simon|last=Collins|publisher=News Letter}} After spending the majority of its time in the [[League of Ireland]] in the Premier Division, the club was expelled in November 2009 when it was discovered there were unofficial secondary contracts with players. It was reinstated a few weeks later but, as punishment, was demoted to the First Division. The club eventually won its way back to the Premier Division.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/northern_ireland/foyle_and_west/8356761.stm |title=Derry City invited back to league |access-date=13 February 2010 |date=12 November 2009 |publisher=BBC Sport }}"}}
